# Why Disclosure Fails

Investors receive more disclosure every year and read less of it. The average 10-K now runs past
eighty thousand words, and Loughran and McDonald (2014) find that download counts for the full
filing fell by a third between 2004 and 2012 while counts for the earnings release rose.

Each new mandate answers a particular scandal and lengthens the filing; none has been repealed since
1996. The Commission's 2016 concept release asked whether the cumulative length impairs readability,
and most commenters said that it does.

Some commenters argue that length is harmless because investors rely on intermediaries. That
argument is not that disclosure works, but that it works through analysts; it predicts that analyst
coverage should offset the decline in reading, which Section 3 tests.
